title: Federal Reserve
html:
Everything the Fed has published since January 2025: what it decided, what it was thinking, and what its business contacts across the country were seeing. Each note links to the official document.

Where we are now (Oct 17, 2026): fed funds 3.75–4.00% after a unanimous hike on Sept 16, 2026, the first since 2023. Chair: Kevin Warsh. Most officials expect one more hike by year-end. Next meeting: Oct 27–28, 2026, then Dec 8–9.

Contents

  • FOMC Minutes Timeline — all 14 meetings since Jan 2025 (decision, vote, key takeaway)
  • Beige Book Timeline — all 15 reports since Jan 2025 (economy, prices, jobs)
  • FOMC Minutes/ — one note per meeting
  • Beige Book/ — one note per report
  • Fed Tracker — running log of rates and odds (in Fed & Macro)

The story in five lines

  1. H1 2025: on hold at 4.25–4.50%; tariffs flagged as a risk to both inflation and jobs.
  2. Sept–Dec 2025: three 25bp cuts to 3.50–3.75% as the labor market weakened; balance-sheet runoff ended Dec 1.
  3. Jan–Apr 2026: on hold; the oil shock from the Middle East conflict stalled the progress on inflation; hawks start to push back.
  4. Jun–Jul 2026: Warsh takes the chair; the easing bias is dropped; three officials dissent in favor of a hike.
  5. Sept 2026: a unanimous hike to 3.75–4.00%; Beige Books show energy costs everywhere and flat consumer spending.

How to use the two documents

  • Minutes come out 3 weeks after each meeting. They show why the Fed did what it did and what it may do next.
  • The Beige Book comes out about 2 weeks before each meeting. It's the Fed's survey of businesses across its 12 districts and an early read on what officials will be weighing.
